- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot upward momentum.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (especially >85) when sentiment is positive and recent prices are rising — model lags in capturing sustained rallies.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.09) and prices are trending up, model underreacts — forecast is too conservative, should be slightly higher.
- Model consistently underestimates the 30-day horizon’s final 5–7 days when sentiment is positive — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is positive and model forecast is >85, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection or inflation of price peaks.
- Mean reversion bias: if model forecast is >85 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overbought signal.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is >10% above 30d history, model often lags — add 0.5–1.0% to forecast for next period if sentiment is positive.
- Sentiment-driven bias: if sentiment >0.44 and model forecast is below 80, increase by 0.5–1.0% to align with bullish sentiment.
